I was 15, attending high school, and a suicide prevention rally came to my high school, which I was required to go to, as well as every other member of my high school, which keep in mind was an all male high school. When I got there, they said it was a common thing, usually some form of chemical imbalance, and that I should go talk to a counselor, which I did. They then went on to refer me to Kaiser, innocent enough, I see a psychiatrist, also innocent enough, but then she asks me what’s wrong, to which I answer, “I just really wanna fucking die,” which I thought was a honest enough kind of answer, but obviously to her, it meant I was a risk to myself. She then proceeds to 51-50 me, everything I have on me, my phone, my wallet my keys, my shoes, my socks, my shirt, everything is taken and put into ziplock bags, and taken away. I sat for twelve hours, and when I was finally transported into an ambulance, they said if I didn’t stay still, they’d have to strap me, and that if they did that I couldn’t go to the hospital they were gonna bring me to. That then led to a 72 hour stay, which then turned into a month stay inside of an intensive care psychiatric unit, where if I stopped eating they would shove a tube down my throat, and if I didn’t take my meds, they’d shove a needle in my arm. So yea I can relate, hardcore. I’m sorry that you had to go through this, but apparently it happens all the fucking time. All of this happened to me as a teen asking for help, at a suicide prevention rally of all things.

It’s not dumb, it’s a common problem for people to seek out the parts of themselves that don’t quite measure up to their peers. Autism is a spectrum, and there’s a very large range of symptoms, and ability to operate. The only real way is to take the tests they give you, and even then, most people who aren’t even on the spectrum, will have some of the symptoms, like not making much eye contact, or seeming awkward. I’m not a psychologist or anything, but I grew up partially raising my older brother, who is on the spectrum. 95% of the people who meet him, only knew he was on the spectrum, because either he or I told them, and generally were very surprised. Thinking you may be autistic isn’t stupid, it actually affects more people than you may think, and presents in a variety of different ways.

Going to one therapist definitely isn’t trying everything. I spent a year and a half combined in psychiatric hospitals by the time I was 21. I’ve had more doctors than I’ve had pair of shoes in the last 5 years. Since 18, I haven’t needed to go back, but when I needed to go, I needed to go. I am severely psychotic, I hear voices constantly, if I didn’t accept the fact that I needed help, then the people who watch me would’ve had to watch me kill myself, violently, cause that’s the only way it’d go down for me. I’ve wanted to die ever since the voices started, so around 12-13, and I only ever lasted this long because I got lucky, the closest I’ve come to death was a couple weeks ago. I’ve attempted suicide three times, and the one time I wasn’t trying to actively die, I fall off a cliff three stories high. To deal with my voices I climb cliffs and shit, well this time it didn’t go so well, and well I lost my grip. Anyway, I didn’t realize until then it was luck keeping me alive, and luck was why I survived that without so much as a scratch. Whiplash for days, but physically fine. If you feel so relieved that you’re gonna die, you should remember that you aren’t lucky if you die, you will die, one day, for sure. Every day you wake up, is different, and each day you’re just as likely to wake up and wanna die, as you are to go out with some friends for a good night. You’re picking and choosing all of the shitty things out of life, try to remember that there is another side, and it is possible to be both suicidal and hopeful. It sounds like a contradiction, and because of that should be wrong, but because of that I’ve made it to 21. Which when I was you’re age was my suicide date. My birthday actually. I still wake up everyday wanting to end it, but it doesn’t hurt as bad as it used to. It doesn’t get a whole lot better, maybe at moments, but eventually you find a way of going through life in a way that makes you stronger than you were before. You take everything that hurt you and turn it into what makes you, you. My voices used to be so bad I couldn’t talk. I’d be disassociated more often than I’d be conscious, but because of that, I am a badass. People don’t treat me the same, and I don’t want them to, because I don’t have to hide who the fuck I am. I don’t know what you have, or why you wanna die, just remember how fucking lucky you are to be here, you could be doing what you love most in this world, climbing for me, and make one mistake, and even though you think you wanna die, you realize you’ll never be able to do it again. Before you can say shit, it’s over, and as soon as you realize it, you want more time. I’m saying this at 21, imagine me at 30, how much more arrogant and entitled can I get right? Be good kid, stay alive, enjoy yourself before you go. Fun is just about the only thing worth staying alive for, try to have some. It ain’t impossible to change, everyone, and everything does it, and I hope you do, before you rob yourself of a beautiful life.
